title: PointZero: 3D Point Track Completion for Learning Transferable 3D Dynamics
abstract: World models endow perceptual systems with the ability to predict how scenes evolve under interaction. They are most beneficial when trained on diverse volumes of data, to instill a rich prior into downstream applications. Existing methods typically require robot action labels to learn action-conditioned 3D dynamics, which excludes web video data from the training pool. We study 3D point track completion as a pre-training objective for learning transferable 3D dynamics without robot data. Given a single RGB-D observation and sparse partial 3D trajectories (tracks), we predict future 3D tracks of all observed points. We show this objective produces a rich 3D dynamics prior, without requiring robot action labels. We contribute a diverse dataset of 2.9 million synthetic frames spanning deformable, articulated, and rigid objects, and use it to train PointZero. We show that a flexible and expressive transformer, PointZero, outperforms prior methods on the same data. We demonstrate the utility of our pre-training objective by post-training PointZero for two downstream applications: (1) action-conditioned 3D dynamics prediction and (2) imitation learning. When fine-tuned to condition on end-effector pose, PointZero outperforms the baselines on the recent PGND 3D dynamics benchmark. When fine-tuned to predict robot actions and 3D tracks, PointZero outperforms or matches the baselines on 6/7 simulated and real-world robot manipulation tasks. We furthermore evaluate training PointZero from scratch to isolate the benefits of our proposed architecture from those of our proposed pre-training objective and dataset. We release the dataset, checkpoints, and full training recipe.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In our seminar on 3D Vision and Robotics, we've discussed a major trend: building large, scalable world models. We've seen approaches like 'Unified World Models' and 'DreamDojo' that leverage massive datasets, often with robot-specific actions. Today's lecture is on “PointZero: 3D Point Track Completion for Learning Transferable 3D Dynamics,” a paper from researchers at Carnegie Mellon and NVIDIA. It explores a different path, aiming to learn a general model of 3D dynamics without being tied to specific robot actions. This is a critical problem if we want to leverage the vast amount of video data available online. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 在我们关于3D视觉与机器人的研讨课上，我们讨论了一个重要趋势：构建大规模、可扩展的世界模型。我们看过像“统一世界模型”和“DreamDojo”这样的方法，它们利用海量数据集，而且往往带有机器人特定的动作。今天的讲座是关于“PointZero：用于学习可迁移3D动力学的3D点轨迹补全”，这是卡内基梅隆大学和英伟达的研究人员的一篇论文。它探索了一条不同的路径，目标是学习一个通用的3D动力学模型，而不必绑定到特定的机器人动作。如果我们想利用网上大量可用的视频数据，这就是一个关键问题。好，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor. So, if it's not using robot actions, how does it learn about cause and effect? Is it trying to learn physics just by watching things move?
segments.zh: 教授您好。那如果它不用机器人的动作，它是怎么学习因果关系的呢？它是想仅仅通过观察物体的运动来学习物理吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the central question it addresses. Instead of conditioning on an explicit robot action, PointZero conditions on a few observed 3D point trajectories. Imagine you see a single point on a towel being lifted. The model's task is to predict how every other point on that towel will move in the future. The core idea is that these sparse tracks provide enough information to infer the underlying dynamics, serving as a kind of proxy for an action without needing the specific, embodiment-dependent labels.
segments.zh: 这正是它要解决的核心问题。PointZero不依赖于显式的机器人动作作为条件，而是以少量观测到的三维点轨迹作为条件。想象一下，你看到毛巾上有一个点被提起来，模型的任务就是预测毛巾上其他所有点在接下来会怎么移动。核心思路是，这些稀疏轨迹提供了足够的信息来推断底层的动力学，从而在不需要具体、依赖具体形态的标签的情况下，充当一种动作的代理。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the main contribution is this new pre-training objective?
segments.zh: 所以主要贡献就是这个新的预训练目标吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. The primary objective is to learn a transferable prior over 3D scene dynamics. The input is a single RGB-D observation, which gives them an initial 3D point cloud, plus one to three complete trajectories for a few selected points. The model then has to predict the future trajectories for all points in the scene. The motivation is scalability. Collecting robot data is expensive and doesn't generalize well across different robots. But videos of objects interacting are everywhere. If you can extract 3D point tracks from them, you have a massive, unlabeled data source for learning about how things move, whether they are rigid, articulated like a cabinet, or deformable like cloth.
segments.zh: 正是如此。核心目标是学习一个可迁移的、关于三维场景动态的先验。输入是一个单帧的RGB-D观测，由此得到初始的三维点云，再加上几个选定点的一到三条完整轨迹。然后模型需要预测场景中所有点的未来轨迹。动机在于可扩展性。收集机器人数据成本高昂，而且在不同机器人之间泛化能力差。但物体交互的视频到处都是。如果你能从中提取三维点轨迹，你就拥有了一个海量的、无标注的数据源，用来学习物体如何运动——无论它们是刚性的、像柜子那样带关节的，还是像布料那样可形变的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Okay, that makes sense. But how does the model actually do this? Combining visual information with specific motion tracks sounds complex.
segments.zh: 好，这就说得通了。但模型具体是怎么做到的呢？把视觉信息和具体的运动轨迹结合起来，听起来挺复杂的。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It is. The architecture is a diffusion transformer. It takes several inputs and learns to combine them effectively. First, it gets the initial 3D position of every point in the scene. Second, it encodes the conditioning point tracks, using embeddings to distinguish time steps and which track is which. Third, and this is a key detail, it uses a pre-trained DINOv2 model to extract powerful visual features from the RGB image. To avoid being overwhelmed by dense image features, it uses a Perceiver-IO module to compress them into a small set of visual tokens. All these tokens—from the points, the tracks, and the image—are fed into the transformer, which then generates the future trajectories.
segments.zh: 是的。这个架构是一个扩散Transformer。它接收多种输入，并学会有效地把它们结合起来。首先，它获取场景中每个点的初始三维位置。其次，它对条件点轨迹进行编码，用嵌入来区分时间步以及哪条轨迹是哪条。第三，这也是一个关键细节，它用一个预训练的DINOv2模型从RGB图像中提取强大的视觉特征。为了避免被密集的图像特征淹没，它用一个Perceiver-IO模块把它们压缩成一小组视觉token。所有这些token——来自点、轨迹和图像的——都被送入Transformer，然后由它生成未来的轨迹。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Why a diffusion model? The report mentioned they also tried direct regression.
segments.zh: 为什么用扩散模型？报告里提到他们也试过直接回归。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Good question. The generative approaches, like flow matching, consistently outperformed direct regression. The authors suggest this is because the problem is inherently ambiguous. Given just one or two moving points, there might be multiple physically plausible ways the rest of the object could move. A regression model is forced to predict a single average outcome, which might not be realistic. A diffusion model, however, can represent a distribution over possible futures, and in their tests, sampling from this distribution produced more accurate predictions.
segments.zh: 这个问题问得好。像流匹配这类生成式方法，表现一直都比直接回归要好。作者认为，这是因为这个问题本身就具有歧义性。只给一两个运动点，物体其余部分可能有多种物理上合理的运动方式。回归模型被迫预测一个单一的平均结果，这可能并不符合实际。而扩散模型可以表示未来可能性的一个分布，在他们的测试中，从这个分布中采样能得到更准确的预测。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: The training data was mostly synthetic, though. How well did this actually transfer to the real world?
segments.zh: 不过训练数据大多是合成的。那它到底在多大程度上能迁移到真实世界呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The sim-to-real transfer is one of their main results. When tested zero-shot on a small, newly collected real-world dataset, PointZero outperformed the baselines on most metrics. This suggests the dynamics prior it learns from simulation is general enough to apply to real objects, even with the domain gap. This is a significant step, because it decouples the large-scale pre-training from the need for robot-specific data. It shifts the field toward leveraging more general, non-robotic data sources.
segments.zh: 仿真到现实的迁移是他们的一项主要成果。在一个新收集的小规模真实世界数据集上做零样本测试时，PointZero在大多数指标上都超过了基线。这说明它从仿真中学到的动力学先验足够通用，即使存在域差距，也能应用到真实物体上。这是一个重要的进展，因为它把大规模预训练和对机器人专属数据的需求解耦了。它推动这个领域转向利用更通用的、非机器人来源的数据。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: This sounds a lot like the philosophy behind other recent papers, like 'μ0' or 'TraceGen', which also use interaction traces instead of explicit actions. Is PointZero's approach fundamentally different?
segments.zh: 这听起来和最近其他一些论文的理念很像，比如“μ0”或“TraceGen”，它们也是用交互轨迹而不是显式动作。PointZero 的方法有本质上的不同吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's an excellent connection. It's part of the same broader movement. The key difference is often in the representation and architecture. PointZero focuses on dense 3D point clouds and uses a diffusion transformer to predict metric 3D motion. It also demonstrates strong transfer to downstream tasks. For instance, after pre-training, they fine-tuned the model for robot-conditioned dynamics and imitation learning. In both cases, the pre-trained model outperformed models trained from scratch, showing that the learned dynamics prior provides a valuable initialization for robotics tasks.
segments.zh: 这个联系非常好。它属于同一个更大的趋势。关键区别往往在于表示方式和架构。PointZero关注的是稠密三维点云，并用扩散Transformer来预测度量三维运动。它还展示了很强的下游任务迁移能力。比如，预训练之后，他们把模型微调用于机器人条件动力学和模仿学习。在这两种情况下，预训练模型都优于从零训练的模型，说明学到的动力学先验为机器人任务提供了有价值的初始化。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the pre-training helps even when you ultimately have action-labeled robot data?
segments.zh: 所以就算你最后有带动作标注的机器人数据，预训练也还是有帮助？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. Even with just 20 labeled demonstrations for an imitation learning task, pre-training on this action-free objective boosted success rates significantly. It suggests this kind of pre-training can make robot learning more data-efficient.
segments.zh: 没错。即使模仿学习任务只有20个带标注的演示，用这个无动作目标做预训练也能显著提升成功率。这说明这类预训练可以让机器人学习更高效地利用数据。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: So, to wrap up, PointZero proposes a practical and scalable pre-training objective. By focusing on 3D point track completion, it learns a general dynamics model for rigid, articulated, and deformable objects without needing costly robot action labels. This allows it to tap into potentially vast sources of interaction video. The main takeaway is this: framing the problem as 'given how some parts moved, predict how all other parts will move' is a powerful, embodiment-agnostic way to learn about physical dynamics. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 总之，总结一下，PointZero 提出了一个实用且可扩展的预训练目标。通过专注于 3D 点轨迹补全，它学习了一个通用的动力学模型，适用于刚性、关节型和可变形物体，而不需要昂贵的机器人动作标签。这使得它能够利用潜在的庞大交互视频资源。核心要点是：把问题定义为“已知某些部分如何移动，预测所有其他部分将如何移动”，是一种强大的、与具身形式无关的学习物理动力学的方式。感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以询问我们的 AI 助手或留言评论。
